# Google MCP Suite Service Matrix

| Tier | Service | Auth Modes | API Client Library | Core Tools (MVP) | Rate-limit Gotchas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Google Drive | OAuth, Service Account (DWD) | google-api-python-client (Drive v3) | search_files, get_metadata, read_text, download, list_children, get_permissions, create_folder | 10 QPS/user; large exports throttled; use fields to reduce payload |
| 1 | Gmail | OAuth | google-api-python-client (Gmail v1) | search_messages, read_message | 250 QPS/user; label/message list rate limits |
| 1 | Calendar | OAuth, Service Account (DWD) | google-api-python-client (Calendar v3) | search_events, get_event | 10 QPS/user; use timeMin/timeMax filters |
| 1 | Sheets | OAuth, Service Account (DWD) | google-api-python-client (Sheets v4) | read_range, get_sheet_metadata | read requests batch; quota per project |
| 1 | Docs | OAuth, Service Account (DWD) | google-api-python-client (Docs v1) | export_text, get_document | export counts as read; large docs | 
| 1 | Meet | OAuth (limited), Admin (recording metadata) | google-api-python-client (Meet/Reports) | list_meetings, get_recording_metadata | Admin Reports quotas |
| 1 | GCS | Service Account | google-cloud-storage | list_objects, download_object, get_metadata | request-based pricing; GCS API QPS |
| 2 | Chat | OAuth, Admin | google-api-python-client (Chat v1) | list_spaces, search_messages | per-minute quotas |
| 2 | Forms | OAuth | google-api-python-client (Forms v1) | get_form, list_responses | low quotas; batching |
| 2 | Tasks/Keep | OAuth | google-api-python-client (Tasks v1) | list_tasks, get_task | per-user quotas |
| 2 | People | OAuth, Admin | google-api-python-client (People v1) | search_contacts, get_contact | field masks required |
| 2 | Admin SDK | Service Account (DWD) | google-api-python-client (Admin v1) | list_users, get_user | DWD + admin quotas |
| 3 | BigQuery | Service Account | google-cloud-bigquery | run_query, get_job, list_tables | job rate limits; per-project quotas |
| 3 | Logging/Monitoring | Service Account | google-cloud-logging, google-cloud-monitoring | list_entries, get_metrics | read quotas; pagination |
| 3 | Pub/Sub | Service Account | google-cloud-pubsub | list_topics, pull_messages | ack deadlines; retry |
| 3 | Cloud Functions/Run | Service Account | google-api-python-client (Cloud Functions v1), google-cloud-run | list_functions, get_service | admin-only; regional quotas |
| 3 | Vertex AI | Service Account | google-cloud-aiplatform | list_models, get_endpoint | high quotas but tight limits |

Notes:
- DWD = Domain-Wide Delegation.
- All services should use scope allowlists and least-privilege defaults.

# Google MCP Suite (Python)

Monorepo of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for Google services with a shared core for auth, pagination, errors, and safety.

## Packages
- `packages/core`: shared framework (auth, client factory, pagination, errors, logging, safety).
- `packages/mcp-google-drive`: Drive MCP server (golden path).
- `packages/mcp-gmail`: Gmail MCP server (search/read).
- `packages/mcp-calendar`: Calendar MCP server (search/read).
- `packages/mcp-sheets`: Sheets MCP server (read-only).
- `packages/mcp-docs`: Docs MCP server (read/export).
- `packages/mcp-gcs`: GCS MCP server (read/list/download).
- `packages/mcp-meet`: Meet MCP server (Admin Reports activities).
- `packages/mcp-admin-sdk`: Admin SDK MCP server (Directory read).
- `packages/mcp-chat`: Chat MCP server (spaces/messages).

## Quick Start
1. Create OAuth credentials in Google Cloud Console (Desktop or Web app).
2. Copy `docs/config.example.yaml` to `~/.google-mcp/config.yaml` and fill values.
3. Install a package locally, e.g.:
   ```bash
   pip install -e packages/core
   pip install -e packages/mcp-google-drive
   ```
4. Run a server (example):
   ```bash
   python -m google_drive_mcp.server
   ```

## Documentation
- `docs/service-matrix.md`: service scope, auth, and rate-limit matrix.
- `docs/config.example.yaml`: configuration reference.
# Google-MCP-Suite

# Google MCP Suite

Eighteen [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers for Google Workspace and Google Cloud, built on a shared core for auth, retries, pagination, errors and write safety. Each server is a small stdio process you register with Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client.

**Write tools are locked down by default.** Anything that sends, deletes, shares or edits needs `confirm=true`, destructive tools additionally need an operator switch, and a single env var turns the whole suite read-only. See [Safety](#safety).

## Servers

| Server | Package | Module | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Gmail | `packages/mcp-gmail` | `google_gmail_mcp` | 12 |
| Google Drive | `packages/mcp-google-drive` | `google_drive_mcp` | 13 |
| Calendar | `packages/mcp-calendar` | `google_calendar_mcp` | 10 |
| Sheets | `packages/mcp-sheets` | `google_sheets_mcp` | 10 |
| Docs | `packages/mcp-docs` | `google_docs_mcp` | 9 |
| Slides | `packages/mcp-slides` | `google_slides_mcp` | 9 |
| Forms | `packages/mcp-forms` | `google_forms_mcp` | 10 |
| Tasks | `packages/mcp-tasks` | `google_tasks_mcp` | 10 |
| People (Contacts) | `packages/mcp-people` | `google_people_mcp` | 9 |
| Meet | `packages/mcp-meet` | `google_meet_mcp` | 2 |
| Admin SDK (Directory) | `packages/mcp-admin-sdk` | `google_admin_sdk_mcp` | 2 |
| Chat | `packages/mcp-chat` | `google_chat_mcp` | 2 |
| Cloud Storage | `packages/mcp-gcs` | `google_gcs_mcp` | 3 |
| BigQuery | `packages/mcp-bigquery` | `google_bigquery_mcp` | 5 |
| Cloud Logging | `packages/mcp-cloudlogging` | `google_cloudlogging_mcp` | 3 |
| Cloud Run | `packages/mcp-cloudrun` | `google_cloudrun_mcp` | 3 |
| Pub/Sub | `packages/mcp-pubsub` | `google_pubsub_mcp` | 4 |
| Vertex AI | `packages/mcp-vertexai` | `google_vertexai_mcp` | 5 |
| | | **Total** | **121** |

Shared code lives in `packages/core` (`google_mcp_core`). Tool names are `<service>.<tool>`, e.g. `gmail.send_email`.

<details>
<summary>Tools by server</summary>

- **Gmail** (`gmail.`): search_messages, read_message, send_email, create_draft, reply_to_message, modify_labels, trash_message, delete_message, mark_as_read, mark_as_unread, list_labels, create_label
- **Drive** (`drive.`): search_files, get_metadata, read_text, download, list_children, get_permissions, create_folder, upload_file, move_file, copy_file, delete_file, share_file, update_file_metadata
- **Calendar** (`calendar.`): search_events, get_event, create_event, update_event, delete_event, list_calendars, create_calendar, add_attendees, quick_add_event, check_freebusy
- **Sheets** (`sheets.`): read_range, get_metadata, update_values, append_values, batch_update, create_spreadsheet, add_sheet, delete_sheet, clear_values, format_cells
- **Docs** (`docs.`): get_document, export_text, create_document, insert_text, delete_text, replace_text, append_text, format_text, insert_image
- **Slides** (`slides.`): get_presentation, get_slide_content, list_presentations, extract_text, create_slide, add_text_to_slide, update_text, delete_slide, create_presentation
- **Forms** (`forms.`): get_form, list_responses, get_response, create_form, add_text_question, add_multiple_choice_question, add_checkbox_question, update_form_info, delete_item, update_settings
- **Tasks** (`tasks.`): list_task_lists, list_tasks, get_task, create_task, update_task, delete_task, complete_task, create_task_list, delete_task_list, move_task
- **People** (`people.`): list_contacts, get_contact, search_contacts, create_contact, update_contact, delete_contact, batch_create_contacts, create_contact_group, add_contact_to_group
- **Meet** (`meet.`): list_activities, get_activity
- **Admin SDK** (`admin.`): list_users, get_user
- **Chat** (`chat.`): list_spaces, search_messages
- **Cloud Storage** (`gcs.`): list_objects, get_object_metadata, download_object
- **BigQuery** (`bigquery.`): list_datasets, list_tables, get_table_schema, query, list_jobs
- **Cloud Logging** (`cloudlogging.`): list_logs, query_logs, get_log_metrics
- **Cloud Run** (`cloudrun.`): list_services, get_service, list_revisions
- **Pub/Sub** (`pubsub.`): list_topics, get_topic, list_subscriptions, get_subscription
- **Vertex AI** (`vertexai.`): list_models, get_model, list_endpoints, get_endpoint, list_datasets

</details>

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and a Google Cloud project.

**1. Create OAuth credentials.** In the [Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), enable the APIs you want (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, ...), then create an *OAuth client ID* of type **Desktop app**.

**2. Write your config.**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.google-mcp
cp docs/config.example.yaml ~/.google-mcp/config.yaml   # then fill in client_id / client_secret
```

Use `GOOGLE_MCP_CONFIG=/path/to/config.yaml` to point a server at a different file. Keep `config.yaml` and `~/.google-mcp/tokens.json` out of version control.

**3. Install.** The servers use the `mcp` 1.x API, so keep it below 2.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e packages/core "mcp<2"
pip install -e packages/mcp-gmail -e packages/mcp-google-drive -e packages/mcp-calendar   # the servers you want
```

**4. Authorize once.** `python authenticate.py` opens a browser for OAuth consent and stores a token in `~/.google-mcp/tokens.json`.

**5. Check a server starts.**

```bash
python -m google_gmail_mcp.server     # speaks MCP over stdio; Ctrl-C to quit
```

## Connect to Claude

Every server runs as `python -m <module>.server` over stdio. Point `command` at the Python inside the virtualenv you installed into (`.venv/bin/python`) so the right packages are found. Replace `/ABS/PATH` below.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add google-gmail  --env GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 -- /ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python -m google_gmail_mcp.server
claude mcp add google-drive  --env GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 -- /ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python -m google_drive_mcp.server
claude mcp add google-calendar --env GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 -- /ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python -m google_calendar_mcp.server
```

Or commit a project-level `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "google-gmail": {
      "command": "/ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "google_gmail_mcp.server"],
      "env": { "GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY": "1" }
    },
    "google-drive": {
      "command": "/ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "google_drive_mcp.server"],
      "env": { "GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY": "1" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop

Add the same `mcpServers` block to `claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`, Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\`), then restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "google-gmail": {
      "command": "/ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "google_gmail_mcp.server"],
      "env": { "GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY": "1" }
    }
  }
}
```

The examples start read-only. To allow writes, drop `GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY`; to allow delete/send/share as well, add `"GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES": "1"`. Registering one entry per server keeps each server's tools and scopes separate; add only the ones you need.

> Avoid blanket auto-approval (`autoApprove`) for write tools. The `confirm` flag is only a speed bump if the client approves every call automatically.

## Safety

All write tools go through `google_mcp_core.safety`:

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1` | Every write tool fails with `read_only`, regardless of the other settings. |
| `confirm=true` argument | Required by every gated write; otherwise `confirmation_required`. |
| `GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1` | Also required for destructive or outbound tools (send, reply, delete, trash, share, move, clear, add attendees...); otherwise `writes_disabled`. |
| `google.allowed_scopes` in `config.yaml` | Hard ceiling on OAuth scopes; anything outside it is rejected (`scope_not_allowed`). |

The agent only controls `confirm`. The two environment variables are set by whoever starts the server, which is what stops an agent from acting alone. Full list of gated tools: [`docs/dev-notes.md`](docs/dev-notes.md#write-safety).

## Development

```bash
pip install -e packages/core "mcp<2" pytest ruff
export PYTHONPATH="$(ls -d "$PWD"/packages/mcp-*/src | paste -sd: -)"
ruff check .
python -m pytest packages/core/tests -q
```

Tests use mocked Google clients, so they need no credentials or network. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs ruff and pytest on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12. The six Google Cloud servers (BigQuery, Cloud Logging, Cloud Run, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Vertex AI) also need their `google-cloud-*` client libraries installed to import.

Known issue: nine packages (tasks, people, slides, forms, bigquery, cloudlogging, cloudrun, pubsub, vertexai) declare `build-backend = "setuptools.build_backend"` in `pyproject.toml`, which should be `setuptools.build_meta`, so `pip install -e` fails for them until that is corrected. Putting their `src/` directory on `PYTHONPATH` works in the meantime.

## More documentation

- [`docs/config.example.yaml`](docs/config.example.yaml): configuration reference.
- [`docs/service-matrix.md`](docs/service-matrix.md): auth modes, client libraries and rate limits per service.
- [`docs/claude-code-setup.md`](docs/claude-code-setup.md), [`CLAUDE_CODE_SETUP.md`](CLAUDE_CODE_SETUP.md): longer setup walkthroughs, including the HTTP-transport scripts (`start_all_mcps.sh`). Those older guides recommend auto-approving every tool; prefer the defaults above.
- [`README_DISTRIBUTION.md`](README_DISTRIBUTION.md), [`DISTRIBUTION_NOTES.md`](DISTRIBUTION_NOTES.md): packaging a distributable bundle.
- [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/): historical implementation status reports (their tool counts are out of date).

## Connect to Claude

Every server runs as `python -m <module>.server` over stdio. Point `command` at the Python inside the virtualenv you installed into (`.venv/bin/python`) so the right packages are found. Replace `/ABS/PATH` below.

```bash

```

Or commit a project-level `.mcp.json`:

```json
      "env": { "GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY": "1" }
    },
    "google-drive": {
      "command": "/ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "google_drive_mcp.server"],
      "env": { "GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY": "1" }
    }
  }
}
```

```json

    "google-gmail": {
      "command": "/ABS/PATH/.venv/bin/python",

    }
  }

```

The examples start read-only. To allow writes, drop `GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY`; to allow delete/send/share as well, add `"GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES": "1"`. Registering one entry per server keeps each server's tools and scopes separate; add only the ones you need.

All write tools go through `google_mcp_core.safety`:

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1` | Every write tool fails with `read_only`, regardless of the other settings. |

| `GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1` | Also required for destructive or outbound tools (send, reply, delete, trash, share, move, clear, add attendees...); otherwise `writes_disabled`. |

+Known issue: nine packages (tasks, people, slides, forms, bigquery, cloudlogging, cloudrun, pubsub, vertexai) declare `build-backend = "setuptools.build_backend"` in `pyproject.toml`, which should be `setuptools.build_meta`, so `pip install -e` fails for them until that is corrected. Putting their `src/` directory on `PYTHONPATH` works in the meantime.

+- [`docs/claude-code-setup.md`](docs/claude-code-setup.md), [`CLAUDE_CODE_SETUP.md`](CLAUDE_CODE_SETUP.md): longer setup walkthroughs, including the HTTP-transport scripts (`start_all_mcps.sh`). Those older guides recommend auto-approving every tool; prefer the defaults above.
+- [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/): historical implementation status reports (their tool counts are out of date).

# Google MCP Suite (Python)

Monorepo of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for Google services with a shared core for auth, pagination, errors, and safety.

## Packages
- `packages/core`: shared framework (auth, client factory, pagination, errors, logging, safety).
- `packages/mcp-google-drive`: Drive MCP server (golden path).
- `packages/mcp-gmail`: Gmail MCP server (search/read).
- `packages/mcp-calendar`: Calendar MCP server (search/read).
- `packages/mcp-sheets`: Sheets MCP server (read-only).
- `packages/mcp-docs`: Docs MCP server (read/export).
- `packages/mcp-gcs`: GCS MCP server (read/list/download).
- `packages/mcp-meet`: Meet MCP server (Admin Reports activities).
- `packages/mcp-admin-sdk`: Admin SDK MCP server (Directory read).
- `packages/mcp-chat`: Chat MCP server (spaces/messages).

## Quick Start
1. Create OAuth credentials in Google Cloud Console (Desktop or Web app).
2. Copy `docs/config.example.yaml` to `~/.google-mcp/config.yaml` and fill values.
3. Install a package locally, e.g.:
   ```bash
   pip install -e packages/core
   pip install -e packages/mcp-google-drive
   ```
4. Run a server (example):
   ```bash
   python -m google_drive_mcp.server
   ```

## Documentation
- `docs/service-matrix.md`: service scope, auth, and rate-limit matrix.
- `docs/config.example.yaml`: configuration reference.
# Google-MCP-Suite

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from google.oauth2.credentials import Credentials


class TokenStore:
    def read(self) -> Optional[Credentials]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def write(self, credentials: Credentials) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError


@dataclass
class FileTokenStore(TokenStore):
    path: str

    def _resolve(self) -> Path:
        return Path(self.path).expanduser()

    def read(self) -> Optional[Credentials]:
        path = self._resolve()
        if not path.exists():
            return None
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return Credentials.from_authorized_user_info(data)

    def write(self, credentials: Credentials) -> None:
        path = self._resolve()
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(credentials.to_json(), encoding="utf-8")

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from google.oauth2.credentials import Credentials


class TokenStore:
    def read(self) -> Optional[Credentials]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def write(self, credentials: Credentials) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError


@dataclass
class FileTokenStore(TokenStore):
    path: str

    def _resolve(self) -> Path:
        return Path(self.path).expanduser()

    def read(self) -> Optional[Credentials]:
        path = self._resolve()
        if not path.exists():
            return None
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return Credentials.from_authorized_user_info(data)

    def write(self, credentials: Credentials) -> None:
        path = self._resolve()
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(credentials.to_json(), encoding="utf-8")

def call_tool(self, *, validate_input: bool = True):
        """Register a tool call handler.

        Args:
            validate_input: If True, validates input against inputSchema. Default is True.

        The handler validates input against inputSchema (if validate_input=True), calls the tool function,
        and builds a CallToolResult with the results:
        - Unstructured content (iterable of ContentBlock): returned in content
        - Structured content (dict): returned in structuredContent, serialized JSON text returned in content
        - Both: returned in content and structuredContent

        If outputSchema is defined, validates structuredContent or errors if missing.
        """

        def decorator(
            func: Callable[
                ...,
                Awaitable[
                    UnstructuredContent
                    | StructuredContent
                    | CombinationContent
                    | types.CallToolResult
                ],
            ],
        ):
            logger.debug("Registering handler for CallToolRequest")

            async def handler(req: types.CallToolRequest):
                try:
                    tool_name = req.params.name
                    arguments = req.params.arguments or {}
                    tool = await self._get_cached_tool_definition(tool_name)

                    # input validation
                    if validate_input and tool:
                        try:
                            jsonschema.validate(instance=arguments, schema=tool.inputSchema)
                        except jsonschema.ValidationError as e:
                            return self._make_error_result(f"Input validation error: {e.message}")

                    # tool call
                    results = await func(tool_name, arguments)

                    # output normalization
                    unstructured_content: UnstructuredContent
                    maybe_structured_content: StructuredContent | None
                                return self._make_error_result(f"Output validation error: {e.message}")

                    # result
                    return types.ServerResult(
                        types.CallToolResult(
                            content=list(unstructured_content),
                            structuredContent=maybe_structured_content,
                            isError=False,
                        )
                    )
                except UrlElicitationRequiredError:
                    # Re-raise UrlElicitationRequiredError so it can be properly handled
                    # by _handle_request, which converts it to an error response with code -32042
                    raise
                except Exception as e:
                    return self._make_error_result(str(e))

            self.request_handlers[types.CallToolRequest] = handler
            return func

        return decorator

import glob
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = "/Users/vaibhaveesingh/Google-MCP-Suite"


def read(p):
    return open(p).read()


def write(p, s):
    open(p, "w").write(s)


servers = sorted(glob.glob(f"{ROOT}/packages/mcp-*/src/*/server.py"))
assert len(servers) == 18

# ---- 1. exact-token rename of tool names everywhere (except docs/archive) -----------------
names = set()
for f in servers:
    names |= set(re.findall(r'name="(\w+\.\w+)"', read(f)))
assert len(names) == 121, len(names)
pat = re.compile(r"(?<![\w/.])(" + "|".join(sorted(map(re.escape, names), key=len, reverse=True)) + r")(?!\w)")

tracked = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard"], cwd=ROOT, text=True).split("\n")
changed = 0
for rel in tracked:
    if not rel or rel.startswith("docs/archive/") or rel.endswith((".png", ".lock", ".zip")):
        continue
    p = f"{ROOT}/{rel}"
    try:
        s = read(p)
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, IsADirectoryError, FileNotFoundError):
        continue
    new = pat.sub(lambda m: m.group(1).replace(".", "_"), s)
    if new != s:
        write(p, new)
        changed += 1
print("renamed tokens in", changed, "files")

# ---- 2. server.py structure ---------------------------------------------------------------
OLD_TAIL = '''    if name not in handlers:
        return [TextContent(type="text", text=f"Unknown tool: {name}")]
    try:
        result = handlers[name](**arguments)
        return [TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))]
    except Exception as exc:
        return [TextContent(type="text", text=f"Error: {exc}")]
'''
NEW_TAIL = '''    if name not in handlers:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
    # Errors are not caught here: the MCP server turns any exception into an isError result.
    result = handlers[name](**arguments)
    return [TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))]
'''
OLD_MAIN = '''if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(main())
'''
NEW_MAIN = '''def run() -> None:
    """Console-script entry point."""
    asyncio.run(main())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()
'''
for f in servers:
    s = read(f)
    for old in (OLD_TAIL, OLD_MAIN, "import json\nfrom typing import Any\n"):
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (f, old[:40])
    s = s.replace(OLD_TAIL, NEW_TAIL).replace(OLD_MAIN, NEW_MAIN)
    s = s.replace("import json\nfrom typing import Any\n", "import asyncio\nimport json\nfrom functools import lru_cache\nfrom typing import Any\n")
    m = re.search(r"def _svc\(\) -> (\w+):\n    return (\w+)\.from_config\(\)\n", s)
    assert m and m.group(1) == m.group(2), f
    s = s.replace(
        m.group(0),
        f'@lru_cache(maxsize=1)\ndef _svc() -> {m.group(1)}:\n'
        f'    """One service per process: config is read once and Google clients are reused."""\n'
        f'    return {m.group(1)}.from_config()\n',
    )
    write(f, s)

# ---- 3. service action labels follow the new tool names -----------------------------------
for f in glob.glob(f"{ROOT}/packages/mcp-*/src/*/service.py"):
    s = read(f)
    new = re.sub(r'(require_(?:confirmation|writable)\("\w+)\.(\w+")', r"\1_\2", s)
    if new != s:
        write(f, new)

# ---- 4. pyproject: console script (+ fix the build-backend typo) --------------------------
for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{ROOT}/packages/mcp-*/pyproject.toml")):
    pkg_dir = f.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
    (srv,) = glob.glob(f"{pkg_dir}/src/*/server.py")
    module = srv.split("/")[-2]
    server_name = re.search(r'Server\("([\w-]+)"\)', read(srv)).group(1)
    s = read(f)
    s = s.replace('build-backend = "setuptools.build_backend"', 'build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"')
    assert "[project.scripts]" not in s and s.count("\n[build-system]") == 1, f
    s = s.replace("\n[build-system]", f'\n[project.scripts]\n{server_name} = "{module}.server:run"\n\n[build-system]')
    write(f, s)
print("done")

"""Server-level behaviour shared by all 18 MCP servers.

Tool names are client-safe, failures surface as MCP errors (isError), the service is built
once per process, and every package ships a working console script. Servers whose Google
client libraries aren't installed are skipped.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import re
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest
from mcp.types import CallToolRequest, CallToolRequestParams

PACKAGES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SERVERS = {
    "admin": "google_admin_sdk_mcp", "bigquery": "google_bigquery_mcp", "calendar": "google_calendar_mcp",
    "chat": "google_chat_mcp", "cloudlogging": "google_cloudlogging_mcp", "cloudrun": "google_cloudrun_mcp",
    "docs": "google_docs_mcp", "drive": "google_drive_mcp", "forms": "google_forms_mcp",
    "gcs": "google_gcs_mcp", "gmail": "google_gmail_mcp", "meet": "google_meet_mcp",
    "people": "google_people_mcp", "pubsub": "google_pubsub_mcp", "sheets": "google_sheets_mcp",
    "slides": "google_slides_mcp", "tasks": "google_tasks_mcp", "vertexai": "google_vertexai_mcp",
}
NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")  # what MCP clients / the Claude API accept


def load_server(module: str):
    return pytest.importorskip(f"{module}.server")


def tools_of(server):
    return asyncio.run(server.list_tools())


def call_via_protocol(server, name, arguments=None):
    """Call a tool the way a client does, through the MCP request handler."""
    request = CallToolRequest(method="tools/call", params=CallToolRequestParams(name=name, arguments=arguments or {}))
    result = asyncio.run(server.app.request_handlers[CallToolRequest](request))
    return result.root


@pytest.fixture
def server_for():
    loaded = []

    def load(prefix):
        server = load_server(SERVERS[prefix])
        server._svc.cache_clear()
        loaded.append(server)
        return server

    yield load
    for server in loaded:
        server._svc.cache_clear()


# --- tool names --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_tool_names_are_client_safe(prefix):
    names = [t.name for t in tools_of(load_server(SERVERS[prefix]))]
    assert names and len(names) == len(set(names))
    for name in names:
        assert NAME_RE.match(name), f"{name!r} would be rejected by MCP clients"
        assert "." not in name
        assert name.startswith(f"{prefix}_"), name


@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_every_listed_tool_has_a_handler(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    service = MagicMock()
    server._svc = lambda: service  # handlers resolve through the module-level _svc
    for tool in tools_of(server):
        asyncio.run(server.call_tool(tool.name, {}))  # raises ValueError("Unknown tool") if not wired up
    assert service.method_calls, "no handler reached the service"


# --- errors are MCP errors ---------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_unknown_tool_is_an_mcp_error(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    result = call_via_protocol(server, f"{prefix}_does_not_exist")
    assert result.isError is True
    assert "Unknown tool" in result.content[0].text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_old_dotted_names_are_gone(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    first = tools_of(server)[0].name
    old_style = first.replace("_", ".", 1)
    assert call_via_protocol(server, old_style).isError is True


def test_safety_failures_are_error_results_not_text(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    server._svc = lambda: server.GmailService(config=MagicMock(), auth_manager=MagicMock(), client_factory=MagicMock())
    # no GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES -> writes_disabled
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_trash_message", {"message_id": "m1", "confirm": True})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("writes_disabled:")
    # operator switch on, but read-only mode wins
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES", "1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY", "1")
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_trash_message", {"message_id": "m1", "confirm": True})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("read_only:")
    assert not result.content[0].text.startswith("Error:")


def test_unconfirmed_call_is_an_error_result(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("calendar")
    server._svc = lambda: server.CalendarService(config=MagicMock(), auth_manager=MagicMock(), client_factory=MagicMock())
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES", "1")
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "calendar_delete_event", {"event_id": "e1", "confirm": False})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("confirmation_required:")


def test_success_is_not_an_error(server_for):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    service = MagicMock()
    service.list_labels.return_value = {"labels": [{"id": "INBOX"}]}
    server._svc = lambda: service
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_list_labels")
    assert result.isError is False
    assert '"INBOX"' in result.content[0].text


# --- service instance is cached ----------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_service_is_built_once(prefix, server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    (cls,) = [v for k, v in vars(server).items() if k.endswith("Service") and isinstance(v, type)]
    built = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(cls, "from_config", lambda *a, **k: built.append(1) or MagicMock())
    first, second = server._svc(), server._svc()
    assert first is second
    assert len(built) == 1


def test_failed_construction_is_retried_not_cached(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    attempts = []

    def flaky(*a, **k):
        attempts.append(1)
        if len(attempts) == 1:
            raise RuntimeError("config not readable yet")
        return MagicMock()

    monkeypatch.setattr(server.GmailService, "from_config", flaky)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        server._svc()
    assert server._svc() is server._svc()
    assert len(attempts) == 2


# --- console scripts ---------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_console_script_is_declared_and_importable(prefix):
    module = SERVERS[prefix]
    (pyproject,) = [p for p in PACKAGES.glob("mcp-*/pyproject.toml") if (p.parent / "src" / module).is_dir()]
    text = pyproject.read_text()
    scripts = re.search(r"^\[project\.scripts\]\n((?:[^\[\n].*\n)+)", text, re.M)
    assert scripts, f"{pyproject} has no [project.scripts]"
    entries = dict(re.findall(r'^([\w-]+) = "([\w.:]+)"$', scripts.group(1), re.M))
    server = load_server(module)
    assert entries == {server.app.name: f"{module}.server:run"}
    assert callable(importlib.import_module(f"{module}.server").run)
    assert 'build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"' in text

"""Server-level behaviour shared by all 18 MCP servers.

Tool names are client-safe, failures surface as MCP errors (isError), the service is built
once per process, and every package ships a working console script. Servers whose Google
client libraries aren't installed are skipped.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import re
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest
from mcp.types import CallToolRequest, CallToolRequestParams

PACKAGES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SERVERS = {
    "admin": "google_admin_sdk_mcp", "bigquery": "google_bigquery_mcp", "calendar": "google_calendar_mcp",
    "chat": "google_chat_mcp", "cloudlogging": "google_cloudlogging_mcp", "cloudrun": "google_cloudrun_mcp",
    "docs": "google_docs_mcp", "drive": "google_drive_mcp", "forms": "google_forms_mcp",
    "gcs": "google_gcs_mcp", "gmail": "google_gmail_mcp", "meet": "google_meet_mcp",
    "people": "google_people_mcp", "pubsub": "google_pubsub_mcp", "sheets": "google_sheets_mcp",
    "slides": "google_slides_mcp", "tasks": "google_tasks_mcp", "vertexai": "google_vertexai_mcp",
}
NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")  # what MCP clients / the Claude API accept


def load_server(module: str):
    return pytest.importorskip(f"{module}.server")


def tools_of(server):
    return asyncio.run(server.list_tools())


def call_via_protocol(server, name, arguments=None):
    """Call a tool the way a client does, through the MCP request handler."""
    request = CallToolRequest(method="tools/call", params=CallToolRequestParams(name=name, arguments=arguments or {}))
    result = asyncio.run(server.app.request_handlers[CallToolRequest](request))
    return result.root


@pytest.fixture
def server_for():
    loaded = []

    def load(prefix):
        server = load_server(SERVERS[prefix])
        server._svc.cache_clear()
        loaded.append(server)
        return server

    yield load
    for server in loaded:
        server._svc.cache_clear()


# --- tool names --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_tool_names_are_client_safe(prefix):
    names = [t.name for t in tools_of(load_server(SERVERS[prefix]))]
    assert names and len(names) == len(set(names))
    for name in names:
        assert NAME_RE.match(name), f"{name!r} would be rejected by MCP clients"
        assert "." not in name
        assert name.startswith(f"{prefix}_"), name


@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_every_listed_tool_has_a_handler(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    service = MagicMock()
    server._svc = lambda: service  # handlers resolve through the module-level _svc
    for tool in tools_of(server):
        asyncio.run(server.call_tool(tool.name, {}))  # raises ValueError("Unknown tool") if not wired up
    assert service.method_calls, "no handler reached the service"


# --- errors are MCP errors ---------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_unknown_tool_is_an_mcp_error(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    result = call_via_protocol(server, f"{prefix}_does_not_exist")
    assert result.isError is True
    assert "Unknown tool" in result.content[0].text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_old_dotted_names_are_gone(prefix, server_for):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    first = tools_of(server)[0].name
    old_style = first.replace("_", ".", 1)
    assert call_via_protocol(server, old_style).isError is True


def test_safety_failures_are_error_results_not_text(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    server._svc = lambda: server.GmailService(config=MagicMock(), auth_manager=MagicMock(), client_factory=MagicMock())
    # no GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES -> writes_disabled
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_trash_message", {"message_id": "m1", "confirm": True})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("writes_disabled:")
    # operator switch on, but read-only mode wins
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES", "1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY", "1")
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_trash_message", {"message_id": "m1", "confirm": True})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("read_only:")
    assert not result.content[0].text.startswith("Error:")


def test_unconfirmed_call_is_an_error_result(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("calendar")
    server._svc = lambda: server.CalendarService(config=MagicMock(), auth_manager=MagicMock(), client_factory=MagicMock())
    monkeypatch.setenv("GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES", "1")
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "calendar_delete_event", {"event_id": "e1", "confirm": False})
    assert result.isError is True
    assert result.content[0].text.startswith("confirmation_required:")


def test_success_is_not_an_error(server_for):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    service = MagicMock()
    service.list_labels.return_value = {"labels": [{"id": "INBOX"}]}
    server._svc = lambda: service
    result = call_via_protocol(server, "gmail_list_labels")
    assert result.isError is False
    assert '"INBOX"' in result.content[0].text


# --- service instance is cached ----------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_service_is_built_once(prefix, server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for(prefix)
    (cls,) = [v for k, v in vars(server).items() if k.endswith("Service") and isinstance(v, type)]
    built = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(cls, "from_config", lambda *a, **k: built.append(1) or MagicMock())
    first, second = server._svc(), server._svc()
    assert first is second
    assert len(built) == 1


def test_failed_construction_is_retried_not_cached(server_for, monkeypatch):
    server = server_for("gmail")
    attempts = []

    def flaky(*a, **k):
        attempts.append(1)
        if len(attempts) == 1:
            raise RuntimeError("config not readable yet")
        return MagicMock()

    monkeypatch.setattr(server.GmailService, "from_config", flaky)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        server._svc()
    assert server._svc() is server._svc()
    assert len(attempts) == 2


# --- console scripts ---------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", sorted(SERVERS))
def test_console_script_is_declared_and_importable(prefix):
    module = SERVERS[prefix]
    (pyproject,) = [p for p in PACKAGES.glob("mcp-*/pyproject.toml") if (p.parent / "src" / module).is_dir()]
    text = pyproject.read_text()
    scripts = re.search(r"^\[project\.scripts\]\n((?:[^\[\n].*\n)+)", text, re.M)
    assert scripts, f"{pyproject} has no [project.scripts]"
    entries = dict(re.findall(r'^([\w-]+) = "([\w.:]+)"$', scripts.group(1), re.M))
    server = load_server(module)
    assert entries == {server.app.name: f"{module}.server:run"}
    assert callable(importlib.import_module(f"{module}.server").run)
    assert 'build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"' in text

---
## Write safety
Every write tool goes through `google_mcp_core.safety`:

- **Read-only mode.** Set `GOOGLE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1` in the MCP server's environment and every
  write tool (gated or not) fails with `read_only`, regardless of `confirm` or
  `GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES`. It covers all of Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Forms,
  Tasks, People and Slides writes.
- **`confirm=true`.** Writes in Sheets, Docs, Forms, Tasks and People, plus Drive `create_folder`,
  need `confirm=true`, otherwise `confirmation_required`.
- **Destructive / outbound tools** need `confirm=true` *and* the operator switch
  `GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1` (e.g. `claude mcp add -e GOOGLE_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1 google-gmail -- ...`);
  otherwise `writes_disabled`. These are: `gmail_send_email`, `reply_to_message`, `trash_message`,
  `delete_message`; `drive_delete_file`, `share_file`, `move_file`; `calendar_delete_event`,
  `add_attendees`; `sheets_batch_update`, `delete_sheet`, `clear_values`; `docs_delete_text`;
  `forms_delete_item`; `tasks_delete_task`, `delete_task_list`; `people_delete_contact`.
- Writes with no `confirm` parameter (Gmail drafts/labels, Drive upload/copy/metadata, Calendar
  create/update/quick-add/create-calendar, Slides) only honour read-only mode.

The agent controls only `confirm`; the environment switches are what stop it acting alone.
`google.allowed_scopes` (see above) is enforced in `AuthManager.get_credentials`, the single
place credentials are built.

## Auth Modes

lastPrompt: stay on fix/sercer-hardening and In every server.py: rename tools from "drive.search_files" style to "drive_search_files" style, return MCP errors instead of "Error: ..." text, and cache the service i…

content.text:
All five changes are in on `fix/server-hardening`. I installed all 18 packages into a fresh venv, and `ruff` and 330 tests pass with none skipped. All 18 console scripts start and exit cleanly. Nothing is committed.

- **Tool names.** All 121 tools are now like `drive_search_files` instead of `drive.search_files`. I renamed them in every `server.py`, the legacy `registry.py` files, the safety action labels, the tests and the live docs. `docs/archive/` is untouched. A test checks that every name matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, that the old dotted names return an error, and that every listed tool has a handler.
- **Errors.** The `try/except` that returned `"Error: ..."` as normal text is gone. In `mcp` 1.30, an exception raised in the handler becomes a result with `isError: true` and the text `code: message`, for example `writes_disabled: ...` or `read_only: ...`. Unknown tools now raise too. Tests check this through the real MCP request handler.
- **Cached service.** `_svc()` is now `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`, so config is read once and Google clients are reused. A failed construction isn't cached, so it retries on the next call. Restart a server after editing `config.yaml`.
- **Token file.** `FileTokenStore.write` writes to a temp file created at 0600 and renames it into place. The token is never briefly world-readable, and an older loose-permission file is replaced on the next save. Tests cover a permissive umask, an existing 0644 file, a stale temp file and a failed write. Nothing else writes the token, so I didn't touch any credential scripts.
- **console_scripts.** Each `pyproject.toml` now has `google-gmail-mcp = "google_gmail_mcp.server:run"` and so on. A console script needs a normal function, so I added `run()` to each `server.py`, and `python -m` now calls it too.

Beyond what you asked:
- **Build-backend typo.** I fixed `setuptools.build_backend` to `build_meta` in the nine `pyproject.toml` files that had it. Without that, the scripts couldn't be installed for those packages. I removed the "known issue" note from the README.
- **CI.** It still puts the service packages on `PYTHONPATH`. With the typo fixed it could just `pip install` everything. That would also run the six cloud servers' tests in CI, which are skipped there today. Want me to switch it?

Things to know:
- **Permission rules.** Any permission or `autoApprove` rule that uses the old dotted tool names will stop matching.
- **Unknown tool with missing config.** `call_tool` builds the service before checking whether the tool exists. On a server with no config, an unknown tool reports "Config file not found" instead of "Unknown tool". It's still an MCP error, so I left it.
- **Docs.** I added a short "Behaviour notes" section to the README covering the points above.
